title: How often a total solar eclipse occurs, somewhere vs one spot (years)

source.name: Five Millennium Catalog of Solar Eclipses
source.publisher: NASA Goddard Space Flight Center (Eclipse Website)

notes: A total solar eclipse occurs SOMEWHERE on Earth roughly once every 18 months (1.5 years). But because the path of totality is so narrow, any ONE fixed spot only sees a repeat, on average, once every 375 years -- a figure originally derived by astronomer Jean Meeus (1982) and commonly cited against NASA's eclipse catalog data; NASA's own 5,000-year mapping of every totality path refines the global figure to roughly 366 years.
